correctness.rationale: Every base-b digit-sum-two number for odd b≥3 is b^j(1+b^t), including t=0; n0 is the product of full nonunit prime powers, so dividing by m is reversible by a large shift j. Concatenation realizes every even digit sum. The odd-prime-power unit group has unique order-two element −1; exact local solution exponents have valuation v2(ord)−1, yielding the common-phase criterion. For the 2-power part, t is odd, and (b^t+1)/(b+1) is odd, giving precisely b≡−1 modulo 2^e. Cyclic group element counting and CRT give all residue formulas. The independent verifier passed 2292 finite-state cases and 250 even-modulus count comparisons; finite tests do not replace the complete proof.

originality.rationale: The question in Phunphayap–Noppakaew–Pongsriiam arXiv:2303.13017v1 §3 Question 1 asks for the exact equality criterion beyond gcd=1, and its 2025 journal Question 3.1 still asks it. The new complete d=2 local-order criterion, synchronized CRT condition and exact all-base-residue counts are not stated or implied by its general obstruction or its sufficient digit-sum-divisibility condition. The 2024 fixed-base-2 Hamming results address a different domain and only share familiar order ingredients. The targeted mathematical-record searches returned unrelated nearby mathematical records. No universal independence claim is made.
residual_risks: A similar equivalence may have been proved earlier in literature indexed under another terminology (minimal digit sum, two-term vanishing sums or modular order) and not encountered in checked sources.
Exact general residue-class enumeration may have an unindexed formulation in finite cyclic-group counting literature.

value.rationale: This is a complete d=2 structural classification of a named published higher-gcd digit-sum arc question, including nontrivial global CRT failures invisible from each prime-power test. It determines the exact density of all good bases modulo every even n, and gives an explicit counterexample (19,70) to the paper’s suggested necessity s_b(n)|d. The class and invariant are natural and the statements apply to infinitely many moduli and bases, not an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
